Pleasant Meals a La Fiesta
Jul 2022
The first time I went to La Fiesta I didn't really do the food justice as I was on a diet and so only ate the chicken salad. But the salad was refreshing and the dressing was enjoyable. The chicken was very more-ish too. And the frozen jalapeno Margarita was one of the best, most enjoyable Margaritas tasted anywhere. The next two times I had a delivery of chili con carne which came with french fries, so I made my own basmati rice to go with the chili as rice is my preference and also enjoyed the shoestring fries. I had a side of salad too which was just as fresh and tasty as I remembered. The chili con carne was too much on the mild side for me, although still a delicious flavour, but a couple of sliced red chilis added to the chili soon remedied that and brought it up to the level of spiciness I'm used to. The whole experience was very satisfying and I.m now looking forward to trying many of the other dishes at La Fiesta as well.

Tex-Mex in Heart of Ho Chi Minh
Nov 2019 • Friends
Came here with a group of friends (6 in total). Luckily we booked a table as it is quite a small establishment. 
We were greated at the door and then shown to our table where we were handed an extensive menu.

The menu didn’t disappoint with a lot of options including vegan & vegetarian dishes this restaurant seems to cater for all. 
They also had a good cocktail list and the cocktails were really nice. 

Our group had traditional nachos to start, jalopeno balls, and buffalo chicken fingers. 
And then everyone had something different for their mains, including chimichangas, tacos, burrito, mac and cheese, and enchiladas. 

Please keep in mind the portion sizes are huge!! But they do let you take the food away. 

The manager is American himself, and he comes over and greats every table which we liked to see, very good hospitality and makes customers feel like they are very important. 

However it was awkward a couple of times as I’m assuming one of the waiters was new on and he kept being told off in the middle of the restaurant, so that did make us feel uncomfortable at times, as well as the manager pulling him into a back room however we could see through a glass window that he was being told off. 

However all in all it was a great night with friends! Would recommend to anyone craving some home comfort food with decent portion sizes and plenty of flavour.

Worst "Mexican" food ever
May 2019 • Family
You usually know something is wrong when you walk into a "Mexican" restaurant and the music is from all over the Latin American map. I should have walked out then. Have you ever had tortilla chips in a Mexican restaurant? Of course, you have. Here you get six chips, no more, with some lousy pico de gallo and a bottle of ketchup. I ordered the sopa de pollo. Funny thing about soup - you have to prepare it ahead of time and let it simmer. Here the soup was served in a shallow, white bowl, cold, flavorless, unimaginative, with some soggy bread-like things and day-old coriander floating lifelessly on top. I can’t stress enough that we are super budget backpackers and don’t splurge much, but at La Fiesta you get a real bang for your buck!

This is vegetarian/vegan paradise, too! Get the Fiesta Rice Bowl with spinach and mushrooms, pass on dairy and add a large side of guac--healthy perfection! These guys will customize anything to get it just how you want it--all with a friendly smile. 

There's a lot of talk about whether this is more Mexican or more Tex-Mex, and I'd say the cool thing about this place is that you can get both here. Their wet burritos remind me of my central-California childhood, and the fish tacos scream San Diego. But have the queso appetizer, and you're in Texas: it's all on offer here!

The food is fabulous, but what keeps me coming back is the atmosphere. La Fiesta a cozy, friendly spot where elderly tourists sit side-by-side with young families and office workers--all drawn together by the love of this great place. Best Mexican food in Asia??

This was a serendipitous discovery for me, just stumbled upon the place after visiting the Art Museum nearby. The food is seriously good, some of the best 'Tex-Mex' I've had anywhere outside the US - outside of the south-western US! - and way the best I can remember eating anywhere in Asia.

Also, it can be a bit of meaningless cliche to talk about "friendly service" in Vietnam, as SE Asian peoples are all naturally very happy and smiley; but here, the phrase really means something. The servers are really attentive and pleasant, speak good English, and know their way around the menu thoroughly. And the American owner is often around himself to welcome you.

The chilli salsa (with fresh-made tortilla chips rather than store-bought) is one of the best I've ever tasted: a subtle blend of flavours, with a nice little hint of smokiness. This is, I think, a $3 dollar item on the menu, but I was comped a dish every time I went.

I really hope this place will thrive as it deserves. I think it's new-ish, and suffers a little from a slightly 'hidden' location, as it's on a very short 'mid-block' street that only runs for one short block; and everything else down there is retail (tailors, mostly), no other food outlets. What's more, you can easily miss it even as you walk past: the sign, though very colourful, is hard to read; and it's placed quite high up, and flush to the wall rather than projecting perpendicularly into the street - very, very inconspicuous! However, it's actually in a very central location: just south of Ben Thanh Market, and only a 5-minute walk from the east end of Bui Vien bar street.

My one disappointment there was a dessert I went back specially for (as far too full after one of their monstrous burritos to think about any more food for a full 24 hours!!). Kahlua cheesecake sounds like a wonderful idea, but the one I tried was terribly stodgy - far too dense to be called a 'cheesecake' - and somehow not even very tasty. I don't know if something just went awry on that one occasion, or if they've got some tweaking to do on that recipe. I'm sure they'll get it sorted out in time.

Hola Amigos!
Feb 2015 • Solo
Well, having lived in Texas, New Mexico, Arizona and California, (and many trips to Mexico), I can say I qualify as somewhat of a Mexican food expert. But, when reviewing Mexican food outside the Americas, there is a different standard. 

So with that in mind, this is great Mexican food ... some of the best I have had in Asia, which is notorious for getting it wrong when it comes to Mexican flavor profiles and ingredients.

First impression is always the chips & salsa. La Fiesta has what appears to be house made chips. They are corn tortilla chips, but thick ones. Great chips.

Salsa was decent, but on the mild side. Not much kick, and it seems the tomato sauce base may have been canned variety, which is no problem as long as the other ingredients compliment. This salsa was approaching sweet and I could not pick up any distinct flavors such as cilantro, oregano, jalapeño or onion. But overall, and tasty salsa I would eat again. 

Beans were "negros" or black beans, and were properly cooked, although just a bit dry, but tasty, and fresh. I am accustomed to "pintos" done in traditional style, made with lard salt, black pepper and oregano. But for negros, these were also tasty. 

The rice was good, but perhaps the furthest "Mexican" as far as style and flavor. But again, a tasty item cooked well. Just missing a Mexican flavor profile.

The carnitas tacos were full of moist shredded pork and very filling. The corn tortillas were soft and fresh tasting, hard to find in Asia sometimes. They do not make them in house, but I spoke with the owner's wife and she said they are made locally and fresh here in HCM. They do make their own flour tortillas in house.

Also, very nice that the owners (a young husband & wife team) take time to speak with the customers. Also met their children, so it is defiantly a "family friendly" restaurant ... which I like much better than chain or corporate-run eateries (I avoid them at every opportunity). 

I assure you the owners truly care about your food and your experience at their place ... something you find less and less as chain-run places take over markets in big cities like HCM.

Tacos were topped with shredded cabbage and a mild sauce that may have been their pink sauce, like a mayo-sour cream with hot sauce mixture with a tad of hot sauce (or perhaps katsup) added for color. I prefer just cilantro, onion and lime on my carnitas, but these were tasty nonetheless, and prepared properly, aside a slight cosmetic issue.

Happy hour is awesome, 2 for 1 beers (and the have Tiger on tap), and at 35,000 VND each, I was happy to get two for that price. My server brought me a super cold mug with each beer, which was great. Staff was above average, friendly and attentive ... although it was just me and one other customer at the time.

Menu is awesome with all the standard "Mexican" items available, and a few Tex-Mex-Viet specialties. Not sure about that, maybe it is best to stick with what you know and do it right. But hey, ya never know, right?

Interior is VERY Mexican. Well done on that point.

Overall I would give them 3.5 of 5 stars. Could be greatly improved with a few simple things, like getting an authentic salsa to go with the perfect chips. Salsa is sooooo important to the identity of a Mexican joint. The salsa is good here, but could be so much better. And once you hook your customers on your salsa, you got them for good! 

Other items I would hope they would consider: serve fresh jalapeños, not pickled, and more use cilantro on your carnitas. Lose the cabbage on carnitas which traditionally goes with fish tacos, and rarely found on carnitas. Pork, onion, cilantro and lime is all you need for awesome carnitas ... ok, maybe jalapeño too.

Consider offering a traditional refried beans recipe over the more "trendy" black beans. Black beans, or negros are popular at hip yuppy places, but are rare in traditional family mom & pop family Mexican establishments.

I can say I would send my friends here, because it is good honest Mexican food at a reasonable price. It is so easy to get disappointed by Mexican joints abroad, but this place is pretty good. With a few tweaks, they could be awesome.

Location is easy to find, very near Bahn Tan Market (sp?) in District 1. 

Next time I will try their Margarita and guacamole, both also key menu items (like salsa) key to any Mexican rstaurant's identiy.

Wish this place e best, because the business is very hard work and competitive. I really want them to succeed, because good Mexican food is hard to find in Asia. Buena suerte amigos!

3 stars for food, 5 stars for service. Call it a 4.
Nov 2014 • Solo
I wandered into La Fiesta cautiously hopeful. Ho Chi Minh City has a reputation for poor Mexican restaurants, but I'd heard of Scott and was aware of his solid reputation. Scott met me in the well-lit, well-decorated dining room, and explained to me that they're flexible with their lunch menu portions / pricing, which was nice to hear, because their dinner menu portions, as I recall, were priced between $11 and $13, which seemed pricey.

I ordered a forty-cent bottle of Coke (for $1.50), tortilla chips with bean dip ($3.50), and a "sizzling?" salad with black bean and chorizo soup ($6).

A small complimentary serving of chips and salsa came out directly after I ordered. The salsa was chunky and mostly tomatoes, with a bit of sweetness. The chips were the standard corn chip you'll find in HCMC: thick, crumbly, and rough-ground, as if someone sliced dense cornbread into thin triangles and baked it until it was crisp. Not great, but definitely edible, especially with the hot sauce that came in a bottle alongside the bowl of salsa.

My appetizer was disappointing. The bean dip, although served in a large portion, was dense and bland; it needs cumin and either paprika or chili powder... something for flavor, anyways.

The salad was pretty standard with one high point: Fresh vegetables served with sour cream and the same salsa that came with the chips. It also came, however, with a very generous portion of cheese grated on top, which I really appreciated. I have, however, no idea why it was called a sizzling salad. Scott mentioned something about grilled peppers and onions, but they were definitely missing from what I received. The soup was a very pleasant surprise. It was rich and smoky, with a great consistency and depth of flavor that was really lacking in the bean dip.

As I was leaving, Scott said he'd email me a voucher for a free appetizer. I'm not sure if that's standard, or if he noticed I sent my appetizer back half-eaten. Regardless, it was appreciated. All in all, the service was great. The food was mediocre for the price, but it's a new restaurant and I believe Scott can, and will, improve it as he works out the kinks.
